summary.text: 西 is the character for “west.” One interpretation treats it as a whole picture of a bird’s nest; an old dictionary links the direction to birds roosting as the sun sets. The graph’s origin and the route to its directional use remain disputed.

formation.text: Pictographic interpretation: 西 is analyzed as a whole graph resembling a bird’s nest, not as a compound of separable modern components. This interpretation is disputed; another proposal derives the graph from an early borrowing of 囟. The westward sense is variously explained as a loan or as a development from the sunset-and-roosting association, with no settled account.

history.text: Graphic records label oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript, and small-seal stages. The supplied seal-script rendering is a modern reconstruction; available evidence does not establish a detailed sequence of stroke changes.

A competing analysis proposes that an early form borrowed 囟 on the basis of ancient sound similarity and later developed into the 西 shape. This remains a reported proposal, not an established graphic history.

uncertainties.text: The nest interpretation and the proposal involving 囟 remain competing accounts; within the nest interpretation, borrowing for “west” and semantic development from the sunset association are also unresolved alternatives. A bag or basket account is reported, but its basis is not established here.
The evidence does not establish the name or pronunciation of any depicted nest, bag, or basket, so it cannot support a sound-based borrowing from such an object-name.

senses.period: Oracle-bone and bronze inscriptions; precise dates unresolved
senses.text: The graph is reported for the western direction in oracle-bone and bronze inscriptions. Individual dated examples are not supplied, so the evidence does not establish a precise first use.

senses.period: Oracle-bone and bronze inscriptions; precise dates unresolved
senses.text: The graph is also reported in place and palace names in these inscriptional periods; the evidence does not establish their chronology relative to its directional use.

The nest meaning is proposed from the graph’s pictorial interpretation and described as an original meaning in one graphic-history account. It is not established as the earliest attested single-character use; that account says the meaning is no longer current.

limitations.text: The evidence does not decide whether “west” was written by borrowing the graph for a similar-sounding word or developed semantically from a sunset-and-roosting association. No individually dated tokens establish the sequence.

overview.text: 西 means “west.” It may picture a bird’s nest, with the west linked to birds roosting at sunset, but that origin and the route to “west” are disputed.
